intent.raw_query: Costa Rica eco-adventure, $2500, zip-lining and wildlife, February 2026 from Miami

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do for eco-adventurers seeking an adrenaline rush above the treetops.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari spotting howler monkeys, caimans, river turtles, toucans, and manatees in their natural habitat. Depending on the season, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the Caribbean beach.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs along lush jungle trails that open onto stunning Pacific beaches.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience
experiences.description: Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest in the shadow of Arenal Volcano, observing exotic birds and wildlife up close. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by tropical jungle — a perfect blend of eco-adventure and relaxation.

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. Trek through pristine old-growth rainforest with a local guide to encounter tapirs, peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four species of Costa Rican monkeys in a truly remote wilderness setting.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Costa Rica
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and travel time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Juan Santamaría International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange a small amount of currency at the airport for immediate needs. Take a budget-friendly shared shuttle or public bus to Aegean Bliss Resort (book in advance via Interbus or Grayline for ~$30-50 vs $100+ private taxi). Check in, freshen up, and explore the beachfront property and surrounding area on foot.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the beach at sunset to get oriented. Grab a casual dinner at a nearby local 'soda' (small Costa Rican diner) to try traditional Casado (rice, beans, plantains, protein) for under $8. Pick up snacks and water at a local pulpería (corner store) for the days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a light snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Airport food court or a quick bite near the shuttle stop — look for a local bakery (panadería) for empanadas and fresh juice (~$4-6).
meals.dinner: Local 'soda' near the resort — try Casado with chicken or fish, fresh fruit juice (~$7-10 total).

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is primarily a travel and settling-in day. Confirm shuttle bookings in advance to save money. Download the 'Waze' app and 'Google Translate' for offline Spanish use. Exchange USD to Costa Rican Colones at a bank or ATM (avoid airport exchange booths for large amounts). Keep your first night light and restful.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early for a self-guided sunrise beach walk along the coastline near the resort. Look for shorebirds, hermit crabs, and early morning wildlife. Pack a light snack from your pulpería purchases. Swim in the ocean or explore tide pools if accessible from the beachfront property.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a budget group tour to a nearby national park or wildlife refuge (ask the resort's front desk for the most affordable local operator). Explore mangrove ecosystems, spot howler monkeys, sloths, and tropical birds. Many local guides offer 2-3 hour nature walks for $15-25 per person.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area and enjoy a relaxed evening. Visit a local market or street food stalls for dinner. Try 'Gallo Pinto' (rice and beans) with eggs — a Costa Rican staple that's filling and cheap.

meals.breakfast: Fresh fruit, instant coffee, and bread from the corner store (~$3-4) or resort breakfast if included.
meals.lunch: Pack a simple lunch from the pulpería — crackers, local cheese, fruit, and water (~$4-5).
meals.dinner: Street food stalls or local soda — Gallo Pinto with egg and plantains (~$5-8).

day_by_day.notes: February is dry season in most of Costa Rica — expect sunny skies and warm temperatures (27-32°C / 80-90°F). Apply reef-safe sunscreen and bring a reusable water bottle. Tip local guides 10-15% if they provide a good experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife spotting walk — hire a local guide for a 2-hour bird-watching tour near the resort area ($15-20 per person). Costa Rica is a birding paradise with over 900 species. Look for toucans, scarlet macaws, motmots, and herons along the forest edge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the nearest beach for a relaxing afternoon of swimming and snorkeling. Rent basic snorkel gear from a local shop (~$10-15 for the day) and explore the reef or rocky outcrops. Look for colorful fish, sea turtles, and marine life.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal using ingredients from a local market (feria) — buy fresh vegetables, rice, beans, and fruit. Use the resort's communal kitchen if available, or enjoy a picnic on the beach. Alternatively, find a beachside 'soda' for a budget seafood dinner.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery — fresh pan dulce (sweet bread), coffee, and fresh-squeezed orange juice (~$3-5).
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar or food cart — try 'chorreadas' (corn pancakes) or fresh coconut water (~$4-6).
meals.dinner: Local soda or self-cooked meal — fresh fish of the day with rice and salad (~$8-12 at a soda).

day_by_day.notes: Ask your bird-watching guide about the best spots for wildlife in the coming days. Many local guides double as eco-tour operators and can offer discounts for multi-day bookings. Stay hydrated — the tropical heat is intense even in the shade.

day_by_day.morning: Take a public bus or shared shuttle to the nearest zip-lining operation. Costa Rica is the birthplace of zip-lining tourism. Budget operators offer canopy tours for $35-55 per person (vs $80-120 at premium operators). Look for 'Midworld' style operations or ask locals for the best value. Most tours include 8-12 platforms through the forest canopy.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the zip-lining adrenaline rush, explore the surrounding cloud forest or jungle on a self-guided trail. Many zip-line operators allow you to walk their nature trails for free after your tour. Look for poison dart frogs, leaf-cutter ants, and coatis.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area by late afternoon. Reward yourself with a cold 'Imperial' beer (Costa Rica's local brew, ~$1.50 at a pulpería) and watch the sunset from the beach. Dinner at a local restaurant — try 'Arroz con Mariscos' (rice with seafood).

meals.breakfast: Early start — eat a hearty breakfast at a local soda before departure. Gallo Pinto with eggs, toast, and coffee (~$5-7).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch or eat at the zip-line operator's café — simple sandwiches and fruit (~$6-8).
meals.dinner: Mid-range local restaurant — Arroz con Mariscos or grilled fish with sides (~$10-14).

day_by_day.notes: Book zip-lining in advance online or through the resort to guarantee a spot and sometimes get early-bird discounts. Wear closed-toe shoes, comfortable clothes, and secure any loose items. Most operators provide helmets and harnesses. Weight limits typically apply (usually under 250 lbs / 113 kg).

day_by_day.morning: Visit a nearby wildlife rescue center or sanctuary. Many operate on a non-profit basis and charge modest entry fees ($15-25) that go directly to animal care. See rescued sloths, monkeys, toucans, crocodiles, and reptiles up close. These centers also offer volunteer opportunities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore a local waterfall hike. Ask at the resort or tourist info about accessible waterfalls within a short bus ride. Many hidden waterfalls are free or charge a small entrance fee ($3-5). Bring your swimsuit for a refreshing natural pool swim.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the nearest town or village on foot. Visit the central park (parque central), browse local artisan shops for souvenirs (bargain respectfully), and try local street food. Look for 'Churchill' shaved ice desserts or 'Helados' (local ice cream) for a sweet treat (~$2-3).

meals.breakfast: Resort area café or bakery — yogurt, granola, and tropical fruit (~$4-6).
meals.lunch: Picnic near the waterfall — pack sandwiches, fruit, and water from the pulpería (~$5-7).
meals.dinner: Town center soda or restaurant — try 'Olla de Carne' (beef and vegetable stew), a traditional Costa Rican comfort food (~$7-10).

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes or sandals with grip for waterfall hikes — rocks can be slippery. Bring a dry bag or waterproof pouch for your phone and valuables. Wildlife rescue centers are excellent for photography — ask staff about the best times for animal feeding sessions.

day_by_day.morning: Take a guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding (SUP) tour through mangroves or along the coast. Budget operators charge $25-40 for a 2-3 hour guided paddle. Spot crocodiles, caimans, herons, and kingfishers in the mangrove channels. This is one of Costa Rica's best eco-adventure experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local organic farm or permaculture project. Many farms near tourist areas offer affordable tours ($10-20) that include tastings of tropical fruits, cacao, coffee, and spices. Learn about sustainable agriculture and Costa Rica's 'Pura Vida' philosophy.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a free or low-cost cultural event — check local community boards or the resort's bulletin for live music, dance performances, or community events. Many beach towns have free salsa or marimba music on weekend evenings.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery or pulpería — fresh bread, cheese, sliced tropical fruit, and coffee (~$4-5).
meals.lunch: Farm tour lunch (often included) or a nearby soda — fresh vegetable soup and rice (~$6-8).
meals.dinner: Beachside casual restaurant — grilled chicken or vegetarian 'Casado' with a local beer (~$9-12).

day_by_day.notes: Mangrove kayaking is best done in the early morning or late afternoon when wildlife is most active and temperatures are cooler. Apply insect repellent before entering mangrove areas. Ask the farm tour guide about buying fresh produce directly to save on food costs for the next few days.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning — sleep in or do a gentle yoga session on the beach (many resorts offer free or donation-based morning yoga). Spend time journaling, reading, or simply enjoying the ocean breeze. This is the midpoint of your trip — recharge your energy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the local area by bicycle. Rent a bike from a local shop (~$10-15/day) and ride along coastal paths, through small villages, or to a nearby beach that's less crowded than the main tourist beach. Discover hidden gems that buses and taxis miss.
day_by_day.evening: Splurge slightly on a nicer dinner to celebrate the halfway point of your trip. Find a restaurant with fresh ceviche — Costa Rican ceviche is made with fresh sea bass (corvina), lime, cilantro, and peppers. Pair with a local craft beer or fresh watermelon juice.

meals.breakfast: Treat yourself to a full resort breakfast or a café breakfast — pancakes with tropical fruit syrup, eggs, and coffee (~$6-9).
meals.lunch: Beachside food stall — fresh coconut water, fruit salad, and a light snack (~$5-7).
meals.dinner: Local seafood restaurant — fresh ceviche, grilled fish, and a drink (~$15-20, a slight splurge for a special evening).

day_by_day.notes: Day 7 is intentionally lighter to prevent burnout on a 13-day trip. Check your budget mid-trip and adjust spending for the remaining days. Inspect your gear — check sunscreen levels, insect repellent, and footwear for the adventures ahead. Do laundry if needed (many hostels and budget hotels offer laundry service for ~$5-8).

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to a nearby national park (Corcovado, Manuel Antonio, Tortuguero, or Arenal depending on your resort's location). Purchase a budget shared shuttle seat (~$20-40 round trip). Arrive early to beat the heat and crowds. National park entrance fees range from $18-20 for foreigners.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the national park with a self-guided trail walk using a downloaded offline map (AllTrails app has free Costa Rica trail maps). Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, three-toed sloths, scarlet macaws, and if near the coast, marine iguanas or sea turtles.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort by early evening. Decompress with a swim in the ocean or resort pool. Prepare a simple self-cooked meal using fresh produce from the local market — rice, beans, sautéed vegetables, and fresh fruit.

meals.breakfast: Early and hearty before departure — local soda breakfast with Gallo Pinto, eggs, and coffee (~$5-7).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch for the national park — sandwiches, fruit, nuts, and plenty of water (food vendors inside parks are expensive — ~$15-20 vs $5 packed).
meals.dinner: Self-cooked or simple soda meal — budget rice and bean dish with salad (~$5-8).

day_by_day.notes: National parks in Costa Rica require advance online reservations (Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación — SINAC website). Book your park entry 1-2 days in advance. Bring binoculars if possible — they dramatically improve wildlife spotting. Start trails early (7-8 AM) when animals are most active.

day_by_day.morning: Join a guided wildlife photography walk with a local naturalist guide ($20-35 for 2-3 hours). Even without a professional camera, a knowledgeable guide will position you perfectly for smartphone wildlife shots. Learn to identify animal calls, tracks, and habitats.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local beach that's known for surf. Take a beginner surf lesson from a local instructor ($25-40 for a 1.5-2 hour group lesson including board rental). Costa Rica's Pacific coast has ideal beginner waves. Even if you've never surfed, most people can stand up within the first lesson.
day_by_day.evening: Join other travelers for a sunset beach gathering. Many budget hostels and beach towns have informal bonfire or beach volleyball sessions. This is a great way to meet fellow eco-travelers, share tips, and find group tour partners to split costs.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit smoothie and granola from a local health café (~$4-6).
meals.lunch: Post-surf beachside snack bar — 'Patacones' (fried green plantains with toppings) and fresh juice (~$5-7).
meals.dinner: Group dinner with new travel friends at a local soda — share dishes and split costs (~$7-10 per person).

day_by_day.notes: Surfing in Costa Rica is best in the morning before afternoon winds pick up. Beginners should stick to beach breaks with gentle waves. Always swim and surf near a lifeguard station when possible. The naturalist guide walk is excellent for learning to identify species you'll see throughout the rest of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore a local chocolate (cacao) farm or coffee plantation tour. Costa Rica produces world-class coffee and cacao. Tours typically cost $20-35 and include tastings, hands-on processing demonstrations, and insights into sustainable farming. This is one of the most unique and affordable cultural experiences in the country.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike to a scenic viewpoint or mirador near the resort area. Ask locals for the best viewpoint trail — many are unmarked but well-known to residents. Bring water, snacks, and a camera. The view of the Pacific Ocean, jungle canopy, and volcanic mountains is unforgettable.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local 'feria del agricultor' (farmers' market) if one is operating nearby (typically on weekends). Buy fresh produce, homemade cheese, artisan goods, and street food directly from local producers at very low prices. This is authentic Costa Rica at its best.

meals.breakfast: Café near the chocolate farm — fresh coffee, sweet bread, and fruit (~$4-6).
meals.lunch: Farm tour lunch (sometimes included) or packed lunch on the viewpoint hike (~$5-8).
meals.dinner: Farmers' market street food — try 'tamales,' fresh empanadas, and tropical fruit juices (~$6-9).

day_by_day.notes: Buy a bag of freshly roasted Costa Rican coffee at the plantation tour as a souvenir — it's much cheaper than airport shops and far better quality. The farmers' market is also the best place to buy handmade souvenirs at fair prices directly from artisans. Avoid souvenir shops in tourist zones which mark up prices by 200-300%.

day_by_day.morning: Take a boat tour through a river delta, estuary, or coastal lagoon. Budget river tours cost $25-45 per person and typically last 2-3 hours. Spot crocodiles sunbathing on riverbanks, Jesus Christ lizards running on water, river otters, and dozens of bird species including anhingas and roseate spoonbills.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a local artisan village or indigenous community cultural center (if available near your resort area). Learn about traditional Costa Rican crafts, balsa wood carving, and indigenous Boruca or Bribri culture. Many communities offer affordable guided visits that directly support local families.
day_by_day.evening: Final big adventure evening — book a night wildlife tour ($25-40 per person). Nocturnal animals like red-eyed tree frogs, kinkajous, night monkeys, and giant insects come alive after dark. A knowledgeable guide with flashlights will reveal a completely different side of the jungle.

meals.breakfast: Early start — hearty Gallo Pinto breakfast at a local soda before the boat tour (~$5-7).
meals.lunch: Post-boat tour lunch at a riverside restaurant — fresh fish tacos or ceviche (~$8-11).
meals.dinner: Light dinner before the night tour — local soda sandwich or soup (~$5-7). Eat early to avoid a full stomach during the night walk.

day_by_day.notes: Night tours require long pants, closed shoes, and insect repellent. Bring a small flashlight or headlamp as backup. The boat tour is best booked for early morning (6-8 AM) when crocodiles are most active on the banks and birds are feeding. Confirm night tour meeting point and guide contact details the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Final full morning of eco-adventure — do a solo or small group snorkeling or freediving session at the best reef spot you've discovered during the trip. Rent gear one last time and spend 2-3 hours exploring the underwater world. Take mental snapshots of everything you've experienced.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin packing and organizing your belongings. Sort through any souvenirs and gifts. Visit any remaining local spots you haven't explored — a hidden beach cove, a viewpoint, or a local neighborhood. Walk through the resort area with fresh eyes and appreciation.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at the best local restaurant you've discovered during the trip. Treat yourself to a full traditional Costa Rican meal — Casado with fresh fish, a cold Imperial beer or 'guaro sour' (local sugarcane spirit cocktail), and finish with 'tres leches' cake for dessert. Reflect on the incredible 12 days.

meals.breakfast: Favorite breakfast spot from the trip — recreate your best morning meal (~$5-8).
meals.lunch: Light lunch — fresh fruit, coconut water, and a snack from the pulpería (~$4-6).
meals.dinner: Farewell splurge dinner — full Casado with fresh fish, local drink, and dessert (~$18-25, your biggest meal of the trip as a celebration).

day_by_day.notes: Use this afternoon to settle any outstanding bills, return rental equipment, and tip any guides or resort staff who made your trip special (10-15% is customary). Check if your resort offers a late checkout option for Day 13 if your flight is in the afternoon or evening. Back up all your photos to cloud storage.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up for one final sunrise beach walk — collect a small shell or stone as a free memento. Do a last swim in the ocean. Enjoy a slow, peaceful breakfast and soak in the Pura Vida atmosphere one last time. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort, storing luggage with the front desk if needed.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, use remaining hours to visit any last-minute spots, buy final souvenirs, or relax at the beach. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 3 hours before international departure. Take a shared shuttle or public bus to Juan Santamaría Airport to save on transportation costs (~$30-50 vs $80-120 for a private taxi).
day_by_day.evening: Airport departure. Browse duty-free for Costa Rican coffee or chocolate at better prices than tourist shops. Board your flight home with incredible memories of 13 days of eco-adventure, zip-lining, wildlife encounters, and authentic Costa Rican culture. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final Costa Rican breakfast at the resort or a nearby café — Gallo Pinto, fresh tropical fruit, and the best coffee you've ever had (~$5-8).
meals.lunch: Light meal near the resort before departure or at the airport — keep it simple and budget-friendly (~$6-10).
meals.dinner: Airport restaurant or food court — a final 'casado' or sandwich before your flight (~$10-15).

day_by_day.notes: Total estimated budget for 13 days (excluding flights and accommodation): $600-900 USD depending on activity choices and spending habits. Key savings tips used throughout: shared shuttles over private taxis, local sodas over tourist restaurants, packed lunches for park days, group tours over private tours, and buying produce at local markets. Costa Rica rewards budget travelers who engage with local culture rather than tourist infrastructure. ¡Pura Vida!

trip_options.title: Classic Costa Rica Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do for eco-adventurers seeking an adrenaline rush above the treetops.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight LH arrives at 13:00. Transit from Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Depending on resort location, transfer takes 1–3 hours by private shuttle or shared van (pre-book for mid-range budget, ~$25–$50 per person).
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront). Freshen up, orient yourself to the property, and take a leisurely first walk along the beach to decompress after the flight. Enjoy the ocean views and get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at the resort's beachfront restaurant. Try a traditional Costa Rican 'Casado' (rice, beans, plantains, salad, and protein) paired with a local Imperial or Pilsen beer. Stroll the beach after dinner under the stars.

meals.breakfast: N/A – in-flight meal
meals.lunch: Grab a bite at the airport or during transit – airport food court or a quick soda (local diner) stop en route (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant – Casado plate or fresh ceviche (~$15–$22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer before arrival. Keep luggage light for easy transit. Exchange some USD to Costa Rican Colones at the airport (USD is widely accepted but Colones help at local sodas). Store valuables in the room safe upon check-in.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning wildlife walk along the beach and surrounding coastal vegetation. Look for scarlet macaws, howler monkeys, coatis, and shorebirds common to Costa Rica's Pacific or Caribbean beachfront. Bring binoculars if available. Guided nature walk with a local naturalist guide (~$20–$30 per person, arrange through resort).
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkeling or kayaking excursion in the nearby coastal waters. Rent equipment through the resort or a local operator (~$15–$25). Explore tide pools for marine wildlife including sea stars, hermit crabs, and tropical fish. Rest and swim at the beach mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a nearby local 'soda' (traditional Costa Rican diner) for an authentic dinner experience. Try Gallo Pinto (rice and beans), Arroz con Pollo, or fresh grilled fish. Enjoy a sunset cocktail on the resort terrace before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort buffet breakfast – gallo pinto, tropical fruits (mango, papaya, pineapple), eggs, and coffee (~$10–$15 included or add-on)
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar – fresh fruit plate, ceviche, or a bocas platter (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Local soda near the resort – Casado or grilled fish with patacones (~$8–$14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Apply reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling to protect marine ecosystems. Ask the resort concierge for the best tide pool timing. February is dry season on the Pacific side – expect sunny skies and warm temperatures (27–32°C / 80–90°F).

day_by_day.morning: Full-day excursion to a nearby national park or wildlife reserve (arrange through resort). Guided hiking tour through tropical dry or rainforest trails. Look for white-faced capuchin monkeys, iguanas, toucans, and sloths. Bring water, insect repellent, and sturdy closed-toe shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the national park visit – afternoon wildlife tends to be active near water sources. Visit a river or lagoon within the park for additional wildlife spotting. Return to resort by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed dinner at a mid-range restaurant near the resort. Try traditional 'Olla de Carne' (beef and vegetable stew) or fresh lobster if in season. End the night with a tropical dessert like tres leches cake or arroz con leche.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – scrambled eggs, gallo pinto, fresh juice, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or picnic prepared by the resort / tour operator inside the park (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant near resort – traditional stew or fresh seafood (~$16–$24 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book the national park guided tour at least one day in advance through the resort concierge. Entry fees typically range $15–$20 per person. Wear neutral-colored clothing for better wildlife spotting. Stay on marked trails and do not feed animals.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart resort early morning for Monteverde (approximately 3–5 hours depending on starting location). Take a shared shuttle service (~$35–$55 per person) – a popular and scenic route that may include a lake boat crossing at Lake Arenal if coming from Guanacaste. Enjoy the changing landscapes from coast to cloud forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Monteverde / Santa Elena. Check in to a mid-range eco-lodge or boutique hotel (e.g., Hotel Belmar, Monteverde Lodge, or similar, ~$80–$130/night). Explore the charming Santa Elena village on foot – browse local artisan shops, chocolate and coffee cooperatives.
day_by_day.evening: Visit a local Monteverde restaurant for dinner. Explore the town's vibrant small-town atmosphere. Optionally, join a guided night walk in the cloud forest edge (~$25–$35) to spot nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, tree frogs, and insects.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure – gallo pinto and coffee
meals.lunch: Stop at a roadside soda or restaurant en route to Monteverde – typical Casado (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Monteverde restaurant (e.g., Restaurante Morpho's or Tree House Restaurant) – cloud forest-inspired cuisine (~$14–$22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The road to Monteverde is famously unpaved and bumpy in sections – shared shuttles handle it well but expect a scenic, winding journey. Arrive with comfortable clothes and a light jacket as Monteverde is cooler (18–24°C / 65–75°F). Book Monteverde accommodation well in advance – February is peak season.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE – Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Operators like Extremo Monteverde or Sky Adventures offer multi-cable circuits with Tarzan swings, rappelling, and Superman cables (~$50–$85 per person). Full safety briefing and gear provided. Morning slot recommended for clearer skies.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve (one of Costa Rica's premier eco-destinations). Walk guided trails through primary cloud forest in search of the resplendent quetzal, three-wattled bellbird, and hundreds of orchid species. Guided 2-hour tour (~$20–$30 on top of $25 entry fee).
day_by_day.evening: Visit Don Juan Coffee, Chocolate & Sugar Cane Tour in Santa Elena (~$35 per person) – an engaging hands-on evening activity learning how Costa Rica's beloved exports are produced. Sample fresh chocolate and coffee. Dinner in Santa Elena afterward.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast – tropical fruits, eggs, gallo pinto, and cloud forest coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the cloud forest reserve café or a nearby soda – sandwich, soup, or casado (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Santa Elena town restaurant – wood-fired pizza, pasta, or traditional Costa Rican dishes (~$13–$20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Zip-line tours require closed-toe shoes and comfortable athletic clothing. Weight and health restrictions may apply – confirm with operator. The cloud forest can be misty and cool – bring a light rain jacket. Book zip-line and reserve tours the day before to secure morning slots. Camera straps or secure cases recommended on zip-lines.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning bird-watching walk in Monteverde – hire a local guide for a 2-hour specialized birding tour (~$30–$45 per person). February is excellent for spotting the resplendent quetzal (breeding season). Visit the Curi-Cancha Reserve as a quieter alternative to the main reserve (~$15 entry, guides available).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and/or the Serpentarium (reptile exhibit) in Santa Elena (~$15–$20 each). These compact, educational wildlife exhibits are perfect for wildlife enthusiasts. Alternatively, explore the Orchid Garden with over 450 orchid species (~$12).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in Monteverde at a restaurant with a view. Try a 'Palmito' (heart of palm) salad, local trout, or creative cloud forest-inspired cuisine. Pack bags for next-day travel. Enjoy a final evening stroll in the cool mountain air.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast – fresh fruit smoothie, eggs, toast, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Café in Santa Elena – homemade soup, sandwich, or empanadas (~$7–$11)
meals.dinner: Mid-range Monteverde restaurant with view (e.g., El Jardín or Celajes) – local trout or creative Costa Rican fusion (~$16–$25 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Bring a telephoto lens or binoculars for bird-watching – quetzals can be elusive. Early morning (6:00–8:00 AM) is peak bird activity time. The Curi-Cancha Reserve is less crowded than the main Monteverde Reserve and often has better quetzal sightings. Book guides the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart Monteverde for La Fortuna / Arenal Volcano area (approximately 3–4 hours via shared shuttle or jeep-boat-jeep transfer across Lake Arenal – the iconic and scenic route, ~$25–$35 per person). Enjoy stunning lake views and the first glimpse of Arenal Volcano.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in La Fortuna. Check in to a mid-range lodge with volcano views (e.g., Arenal Observatory Lodge, Nayara Springs area lodges, or similar, ~$90–$150/night). Relax at the hotel pool or take a short walk to La Fortuna Waterfall viewpoint to plan the next day's visit.
day_by_day.evening: Explore La Fortuna town – a lively hub with restaurants, souvenir shops, and tour operators. Enjoy dinner at a local restaurant with Arenal Volcano backdrop. Browse the evening market if available.

meals.breakfast: Eco-lodge breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Riverside or lakeside soda during jeep-boat-jeep transfer stop (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: La Fortuna town restaurant (e.g., Restaurante Nene's or Don Rufino) – grilled meats, casado, or fresh river fish (~$14–$22 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The jeep-boat-jeep transfer is a classic Costa Rica experience and highly recommended over the longer road route. Book in advance through your Monteverde hotel. La Fortuna is warmer and more humid than Monteverde (25–32°C / 77–90°F) – adjust clothing accordingly. Arenal Volcano is occasionally cloud-covered; morning views are typically clearest.

day_by_day.morning: Hike to La Fortuna Waterfall – a stunning 70-meter cascade accessible via a 500-step descent (~$20 entry). Swim in the natural pool at the base. The surrounding forest is rich with wildlife including toucans, hummingbirds, and howler monkeys. Arrive early to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano National Park hiking – guided walk on lava fields and forest trails with volcano views (~$15 park entry + $25–$35 guide). Spot wildlife including coatis, deer, and diverse bird species. Return to lodge for rest before evening.
day_by_day.evening: Soak in natural hot springs near Arenal – choose from mid-range options like Tabacón (premium, ~$60–$80) or Eco Termales (more intimate, ~$38–$45, reservations required). Thermal mineral waters are naturally heated by the volcano. Dinner at the hot springs restaurant or back in La Fortuna.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – gallo pinto, tropical fruits, eggs, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch near the waterfall or a local soda in La Fortuna (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Hot springs restaurant or La Fortuna town – grilled chicken, fresh fish, or vegetarian casado (~$14–$20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear swimwear under clothes for the waterfall swim and hot springs. Bring water shoes for the waterfall pool. The descent to La Fortuna Waterfall is steep – take your time and wear sturdy shoes. Eco Termales requires advance reservations and limits visitor numbers for a more peaceful experience – book 1–2 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: White-water rafting on the Sarapiquí or Balsa River – Class II–III rapids suitable for all skill levels (~$55–$75 per person including equipment, guide, and transport). Excellent wildlife spotting from the river including kingfishers, herons, caimans, and river otters. Full safety briefing provided.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Arenal Hanging Bridges (Mistico Arenal Hanging Bridges Park) – a 3km trail with 16 bridges (6 hanging) through primary rainforest canopy (~$24 entry). Spot monkeys, sloths, toucans, and countless plant species. Self-guided or with a naturalist guide (~$30 additional).
day_by_day.evening: Cooking class or cultural experience in La Fortuna – learn to prepare traditional Costa Rican dishes like gallo pinto, tamales, or ceviche with a local family or cooking school (~$45–$65 per person including meal). A fun and delicious way to connect with local culture.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast – fresh smoothie, eggs, gallo pinto, and coffee
meals.lunch: Post-rafting lunch provided by tour operator OR quick soda stop in La Fortuna (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Cooking class meal (included) OR La Fortuna restaurant – try local specialty 'Chifrijo' (rice, beans, pork, and pico de gallo) (~$12–$18 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Wear clothes you don't mind getting wet for rafting – synthetic quick-dry fabrics are ideal. Secure all valuables in waterproof bags. The hanging bridges are best in the morning when wildlife is most active – consider swapping afternoon/morning activities if possible. Book rafting and cooking class at least one day in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Wildlife boat tour on Lake Arenal or the Caño Negro Wildlife Refuge (if day-trip distance allows) – spot caimans, river turtles, roseate spoonbills, jabiru storks, and Jesus Christ lizards. Guided boat tours from La Fortuna to Caño Negro take approximately 2 hours each way (~$55–$75 per person including transport and guide).
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from wildlife tour. Visit a local chocolate farm or coffee plantation near La Fortuna for an educational tour (~$25–$35). Learn about the bean-to-bar process and sample artisan chocolate. Alternatively, enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the lodge pool.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset horseback riding near Arenal Volcano (~$45–$65 per person, 2-hour guided ride). Watch the volcano glow against the evening sky from horseback. Dinner at lodge or La Fortuna town afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early lodge breakfast before wildlife tour departure
meals.lunch: Lunch included in Caño Negro tour OR packed lunch from lodge (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Lodge restaurant or La Fortuna – 'Sopa Negra' (black bean soup) or grilled tilapia with rice and salad (~$14–$20 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Caño Negro is a full-day excursion – confirm logistics and timing with your tour operator. February is excellent for bird-watching at Caño Negro as migratory birds are present. Bring binoculars, zoom camera, and plenty of insect repellent for the boat tour. Horseback riding operators should be vetted for animal welfare standards – ask the concierge for responsible operators.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Depart La Fortuna for Manuel Antonio or return to the Pacific coast / Aegean Bliss Resort (approximately 3.5–5 hours by shared shuttle). Alternatively, if Aegean Bliss Resort is in the Guanacaste region, travel back north (~3–4 hours). Enjoy the scenic drive through Costa Rica's central valley and countryside.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive back at Aegean Bliss Resort (Beachfront). Re-check in and decompress. Enjoy the beach, pool, and resort amenities. Take a gentle afternoon swim or paddleboard session to transition back to coastal relaxation mode.
day_by_day.evening: Beachfront dinner at the resort or a nearby restaurant. Enjoy fresh seafood – grilled mahi-mahi, shrimp in garlic sauce, or a whole red snapper. Watch the sunset over the Pacific and reflect on the week's adventures.

meals.breakfast: Lodge breakfast before departure – gallo pinto, eggs, and coffee
meals.lunch: Roadside soda or restaurant stop en route (~$8–$12)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant at or near Aegean Bliss Resort – fresh grilled seafood platter (~$18–$28 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the shared shuttle from La Fortuna back to your resort area. Shared shuttles are the most cost-effective option (~$35–$55 per person). If budget allows, a domestic flight (e.g., Sansa Airlines from Arenal/La Fortuna to Liberia or Quepos) saves significant travel time (~$80–$120 per person). Confirm resort check-in time and arrange luggage storage if arriving early.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise beach yoga or meditation session on the resort beach (offered by many beachfront resorts, ~$15–$20 per person or free for guests). Follow with a relaxed morning swim and snorkeling along the reef or rocky coastal outcrops. Look for sea turtles, rays, and tropical fish.
day_by_day.afternoon: Sport fishing charter or whale/dolphin watching boat tour departing from the nearest marina (~$65–$95 per person for dolphin/whale watching; ~$150–$250 for sportfishing). February is excellent for spotting humpback whales, spinner dolphins, and diverse marine wildlife along Costa Rica's Pacific coast.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell beach bonfire (arrange through resort) or a sunset cruise along the coastline (~$45–$65 per person, includes drinks and snacks). Final dinner at the resort's signature restaurant – splurge slightly on the last night with a surf-and-turf or fresh lobster dish.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast – açaí bowl, tropical fruit platter, granola, and fresh juice
meals.lunch: Light beach lunch – ceviche, fish tacos, and fresh coconut water at the resort beach bar (~$10–$15)
meals.dinner: Resort signature restaurant – lobster, surf-and-turf, or fresh catch of the day (~$22–$35 per person, slight splurge for final night)

day_by_day.notes: Book the dolphin/whale watching or sportfishing tour the day before to secure spots. February is peak season for humpback whale sightings on the Pacific coast. The sunset cruise is a magical way to end the trip – many operators include light appetizers and a drink. Pack sunscreen, hat, and camera for the boat tour.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Costa Rica. Wake up early for one last sunrise beach walk and wildlife spotting – look for nesting sea turtles (if in season), shorebirds, and the inevitable howler monkey chorus. Pack and prepare for checkout. Grab a final cup of Costa Rican coffee on the resort terrace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) or Liberia International Airport (LIR) depending on departure flight. Allow 3–4 hours for the transfer plus airport check-in. Browse airport duty-free for last-minute souvenirs – Costa Rican coffee, chocolate, and artisan goods make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Costa Rica. Reflect on 13 incredible days of zip-lining through cloud forests, wildlife encounters, volcanic hot springs, and beachfront relaxation. Pura Vida!

meals.breakfast: Final resort breakfast – full Costa Rican spread with gallo pinto, eggs, fresh tropical fruits, and that last perfect cup of Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at airport or en route – airport café or a final soda stop (~$8–$14)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport restaurant if late departure

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange airport transfer the night before – confirm pickup time with driver or shuttle company. Allow extra time for the airport journey during peak season. Declare any agricultural products (coffee, fruits) at customs – pre-packaged sealed coffee is fine to bring home. Exit tax is typically included in airline tickets but confirm in advance. Say 'Pura Vida' to everyone you meet on the way out – it's the Costa Rican way of life!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Costa Rica Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour
experiences.description: Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits, featuring over 10 cables, Tarzan swings, and breathtaking views of the Monteverde reserve. A must-do for eco-adventurers seeking an adrenaline rush above the treetops.

experiences.name: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari
experiences.description: Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari spotting howler monkeys, caimans, river turtles, toucans, and manatees in their natural habitat. Depending on the season, witness the awe-inspiring nesting of green sea turtles on the Caribbean beach.

experiences.name: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike
experiences.description: Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide who will help you spot sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and poison dart frogs along lush jungle trails that open onto stunning Pacific beaches.

experiences.name: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience
experiences.description: Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest in the shadow of Arenal Volcano, observing exotic birds and wildlife up close. End the day soaking in natural volcanic hot spring pools surrounded by tropical jungle — a perfect blend of eco-adventure and relaxation.

experiences.name: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Day Trek with Naturalist Guide
experiences.description: Venture deep into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. Trek through pristine old-growth rainforest with a local guide to encounter tapirs, peccaries, harpy eagles, and all four species of Costa Rican monkeys in a truly remote wilderness setting.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer via luxury SUV to Aegean Bliss Resort. Upon arrival, enjoy a welcome cocktail and resort orientation. Settle into your beachfront suite and take a leisurely stroll along the private beach to decompress from travel.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the resort's oceanfront bar followed by a private welcome dinner on the beach terrace. Enjoy a curated tasting menu featuring fresh Costa Rican ceviche, grilled pargo (red snapper), and tropical fruit desserts paired with local craft cocktails.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: Light snack or airport lounge meal prior to departure / during layover
meals.dinner: Private welcome dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront restaurant — Chef's tasting menu with fresh Pacific seafood and tropical specialties

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. Request early check-in if possible. Keep Day 1 relaxed to adjust to the time zone. Ask resort concierge to confirm all upcoming excursion bookings and logistics.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach led by the resort's private wellness instructor, followed by a hearty gourmet breakfast at the resort's main restaurant overlooking the Pacific Ocean.
day_by_day.afternoon: Manuel Antonio National Park Guided Wildlife Hike — Explore one of the world's most biodiverse national parks with a certified naturalist guide. Spot three-toed sloths, white-faced capuchin monkeys, scarlet macaws, and rare poison dart frogs. The park is located within easy reach of the beachfront resort area.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort for a freshwater plunge pool soak and spa treatment. Dinner at a premium local restaurant in Manuel Antonio town featuring farm-to-table Costa Rican cuisine with ocean views.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast buffet at Aegean Bliss Resort — tropical fruits, eggs Benedict, freshly baked pastries, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Picnic-style gourmet lunch box prepared by the resort and enjoyed inside Manuel Antonio National Park at a scenic overlook
meals.dinner: La Luna Restaurant or equivalent premium restaurant in Manuel Antonio — grilled local fish, plantain-crusted chicken, and artisanal desserts

day_by_day.notes: Manuel Antonio National Park has limited daily visitor capacity — ensure tickets are pre-booked through the resort concierge. Bring biodegradable sunscreen, insect repellent, and binoculars for wildlife spotting. Wear light, breathable hiking attire.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking or stand-up paddleboarding session along the resort's beachfront coastline with a certified water sports instructor. Explore hidden coves and spot marine wildlife including pelicans and sea turtles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon at the resort — enjoy the infinity pool, beachside cabana service, or book a 90-minute couples' massage at the resort spa. Optional: snorkeling excursion in the nearby coral reef with private guide.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset sailing catamaran cruise along the Pacific coast with onboard canapés, champagne, and a live acoustic guitarist. Watch for dolphins and humpback whales (seasonal) as the sun dips below the horizon.

meals.breakfast: À la carte breakfast in bed or on your private terrace — avocado toast, tropical smoothie bowls, and fresh Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at the resort's casual poolside grill — ceviche, grilled shrimp tacos, and fresh coconut water
meals.dinner: Onboard canapés and tapas during the sunset sailing cruise, followed by a light late dinner at the resort's wine bar

day_by_day.notes: Sunset sailing catamaran cruises typically depart around 16:00–16:30. Book through the resort concierge at least 24 hours in advance. February is prime humpback whale season in Costa Rica's Pacific coast — request a whale-watching focus from your captain.

day_by_day.morning: Private transfer departs early (06:00) for the Osa Peninsula — approximately a 2.5 to 3-hour scenic drive through lush rainforest and coastal roads. Arrive at the Corcovado National Park ranger station for a pre-arranged guided entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Osa Peninsula Corcovado Day Trek with Naturalist Guide — Venture deep into Corcovado National Park, described by National Geographic as the most biologically intense place on Earth. Trek through primary rainforest alongside a certified naturalist guide spotting tapirs, jaguars (rare), scarlet macaws, poison dart frogs, and four species of monkeys. Swim in a freshwater river inside the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the resort. Enjoy a restorative hot stone massage or hydrotherapy session at the resort spa upon return. Relaxed dinner at the resort highlighting Osa-inspired jungle flavors.

meals.breakfast: Early grab-and-go gourmet breakfast box prepared by the resort — energy bars, tropical fruit, sandwiches, and thermos of Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed lunch enjoyed in Corcovado National Park — fresh sandwiches, local cheeses, tropical fruits, and cold-pressed juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant — jungle-to-table tasting menu featuring heart of palm, local game, and exotic fruit sorbets

day_by_day.notes: Corcovado National Park requires advance permits and a certified guide by law — all arrangements should be confirmed through the resort concierge. Wear sturdy, waterproof hiking boots. The trek involves river crossings and uneven terrain. Bring a dry bag for electronics. This is a full and physically demanding day.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning at the resort. Gentle stretching or meditation session with the resort wellness instructor on the beach. Leisurely late breakfast enjoyed on your private terrace with panoramic ocean views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private horseback riding tour through coastal rainforest trails and along the beach with a local expert guide. Spot wildlife including iguanas, toucans, and coastal birds. End the ride with a refreshing ocean dip.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private chef dinner experience in your beachfront suite or on a private stretch of beach. A resort chef prepares a five-course Costa Rican tasting menu tableside, paired with premium wines from an international cellar.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely à la carte breakfast on private terrace — eggs any style, fresh tropical fruits, artisanal breads, and specialty Costa Rican pour-over coffee
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch at the resort — grilled fish of the day, quinoa salad, and fresh-pressed tropical juices
meals.dinner: Private five-course chef's dinner in your suite or on the beach — Costa Rican lobster, wagyu beef tenderloin, artisanal cheese board, and chocolate lava cake with local cacao

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book the private chef dinner experience at least 48 hours in advance through the resort concierge. Specify any dietary restrictions or preferences. The horseback riding excursion is suitable for all skill levels — inform the guide of your experience level beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Depart resort at 05:30 for a full-day journey to the Arenal Volcano region via private luxury vehicle (approximately 4–4.5 hours). Enjoy a scenic drive through Costa Rica's diverse landscapes — coffee plantations, cloud forests, and volcanic highlands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arenal Volcano Hanging Bridges & Hot Springs Experience — Walk a series of suspension bridges through primary rainforest in the shadow of Arenal Volcano, observing canopy wildlife, exotic birds, and lush flora. Transition to a premium private hot springs resort (Tabacón Grand Spa or equivalent) for an afternoon of volcanic thermal pools surrounded by tropical gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at a premier Arenal restaurant overlooking the volcano. Enjoy the glow of Arenal's lava fields after dark (weather permitting) from a scenic viewpoint before checking into a luxury Arenal lodge for the night.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort before departure — continental spread with fresh fruits, pastries, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Gourmet lunch at Tabacón Grand Spa or equivalent hot springs resort restaurant — fresh salads, grilled meats, and tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Dinner at Don Rufino Restaurant or equivalent premium Arenal restaurant — wood-fired steaks, local trout, and Costa Rican craft beer pairings

day_by_day.notes: This is a transition day from the coastal resort to the Arenal region. Pre-book a luxury lodge near Arenal Volcano — recommended options include Nayara Springs, Tabacón Thermal Resort & Spa, or The Springs Resort & Spa. Confirm hot springs access and hanging bridges tour times in advance. Pack layers as Arenal can be cooler and rainier than the coast.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided wildlife walk around the Arenal Volcano National Park perimeter at dawn — the best time to spot toucans, morpho butterflies, coatis, and sloths in the primary forest. Enjoy the dramatic views of the volcano cone at sunrise.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure afternoon at the luxury Arenal lodge — enjoy the private volcanic hot springs, infinity pool, and spa facilities. Optional: white-water rafting on the Balsa River (Class II–III) with a private guide for an adrenaline boost.
day_by_day.evening: Private stargazing experience on the lodge grounds with a local astronomy guide. Costa Rica's low light pollution and clear February skies make for spectacular celestial viewing. End the evening with a nightcap of aged Costa Rican rum by the fire pit.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Arenal luxury lodge — fresh tropical fruits, gallo pinto (traditional rice and beans), eggs, and local coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the lodge — grilled chicken, ceviche, and fresh tropical fruit platters
meals.dinner: Dinner at the lodge's fine dining restaurant — multi-course Costa Rican fusion menu featuring local ingredients paired with premium wines

day_by_day.notes: The Arenal Volcano is most visible in the early morning before clouds roll in — prioritize the sunrise wildlife walk. White-water rafting should be booked through the lodge concierge and is weather-dependent. Pack a light jacket and rain layer for all Arenal activities.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Arenal early (06:00) for Monteverde — approximately a 3-hour scenic mountain drive through the Tilaran mountain range. Arrive in Monteverde and check into a premium cloud forest lodge (Santa Elena or Monteverde area).
day_by_day.afternoon: Monteverde Cloud Forest Zip-Line Canopy Tour — Soar through the misty cloud forest canopy on one of Costa Rica's most thrilling zip-line circuits. Experience 10+ platforms, Tarzan swings, and a Superman-style cable stretching over a kilometer through the treetops. The cloud forest mist creates an ethereal, otherworldly atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Monteverde Cheese Factory (La Lechería) for a private artisanal cheese and wine tasting — Monteverde is famous for its dairy heritage brought by Quaker settlers. Evening guided night walk through the cloud forest to spot nocturnal wildlife including kinkajous, tarantulas, and glass frogs.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Arenal lodge before departure — grab-and-go option available
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium Monteverde restaurant upon arrival — Café Colibri or Trio Restaurant — featuring cloud forest-inspired dishes and organic local produce
meals.dinner: Dinner at Celajes Restaurant at Hotel Belmar or equivalent premium Monteverde restaurant — farm-to-table tasting menu with panoramic cloud forest views

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Arenal to Monteverde includes a section of unpaved mountain road — a 4WD vehicle is essential. The zip-line tour typically lasts 3–4 hours including transfers. Book the night walk through the lodge concierge — groups are small and private options are available. Temperatures in Monteverde average 18–22°C — pack a light fleece and waterproof jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided birdwatching tour in the Monteverde Cloud Forest Biological Reserve at dawn — home to over 400 bird species including the resplendent quetzal (most visible February–April). A certified ornithologist guide will lead the 3-hour walk through pristine primary cloud forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Santa Elena Cloud Forest Reserve on a self-guided or guided afternoon walk. Visit the Monteverde Butterfly Garden and Hummingbird Gallery — home to dozens of hummingbird species that feed at close range. Browse artisan galleries and local craft shops in the Santa Elena village.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive frog and reptile night tour at the Ranario (Frog Pond of Monteverde) with a private naturalist guide. See over 25 frog species including the iconic red-eyed tree frog up close. Return to the lodge for a nightcap and stargazing from the cloud forest viewpoint.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at the lodge before the birdwatching tour — fresh fruit, yogurt, and Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch in Santa Elena village at Morpho's Restaurant or equivalent — casado (traditional Costa Rican plate), fresh juices, and local desserts
meals.dinner: Private in-lodge dinner experience at the premium cloud forest lodge — chef's special featuring organic vegetables, local cheeses, and Costa Rican beef

day_by_day.notes: The resplendent quetzal is one of the world's most sought-after birds — February and March are peak nesting season in Monteverde, making this an exceptional time for sightings. Bring high-quality binoculars and a camera with a telephoto lens. The birdwatching tour should be booked with a specialized ornithologist guide through the lodge.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Monteverde at 07:00 for Tortuguero on the Caribbean coast — a full-day journey involving a private vehicle transfer to the Sarapiquí River, followed by a scenic 2-hour river boat ride through jungle waterways to reach the remote Tortuguero village. Check into a premium eco-lodge (Tortuga Lodge or equivalent).
day_by_day.afternoon: Tortuguero National Park Wildlife River Safari — Glide through the jungle waterways of Tortuguero on a guided boat safari spotting howler monkeys, caimans, green sea turtles, manatees, river otters, and an extraordinary array of tropical birds including toucans and kingfishers.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into the eco-lodge and enjoy a welcome cocktail on the riverside terrace. Dinner at the lodge's premium restaurant overlooking the jungle canopy and river. Optional evening walk along Tortuguero beach (guided) to observe nesting sea turtles (note: February is not peak nesting season, but leatherback turtles begin arriving).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Monteverde lodge before early departure — full hot breakfast with eggs, gallo pinto, fresh fruits, and coffee
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch box enjoyed during the river boat transfer to Tortuguero
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tortuga Lodge's riverside restaurant or equivalent — Caribbean-influenced Costa Rican cuisine featuring coconut rice, fresh river fish, and plantains

day_by_day.notes: Tortuguero is accessible only by boat or small plane — no roads connect the village. The transfer from Monteverde to Tortuguero is a long travel day (8–10 hours total). Consider arranging a private charter flight from San José to Tortuguero airstrip (30 minutes) as a premium alternative to save time. Confirm lodge arrangements well in advance as Tortuguero has limited luxury accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn guided sea turtle beach patrol (05:00) with a licensed Tortuguero guide — leatherback sea turtles begin nesting in February and early March. Walk the protected beach in small groups under red-light conditions to observe nesting behavior without disturbing the turtles. Return for a full breakfast at the lodge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private guided kayaking tour through Tortuguero's secondary jungle canals — the most intimate way to explore the waterways and spot shy wildlife including Jesus Christ lizards (basilisks), freshwater turtles, and tropical birds. Alternatively, a canopy hiking trail walk through the national park with a naturalist guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise along the main Tortuguero canal with champagne and canapés. Spot caimans emerging at dusk and listen to the chorus of the jungle nightlife. Return to the lodge for a leisurely dinner and a live marimba music performance.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the lodge after the early morning turtle patrol — eggs, fresh tropical fruits, Costa Rican coffee, and freshly baked bread
meals.lunch: Lunch at the lodge — Caribbean rice and beans (rice cooked in coconut milk), grilled fish, and fresh tropical fruit juices
meals.dinner: Premium dinner at the lodge restaurant — Caribbean lobster, plantain-crusted sea bass, and exotic fruit desserts paired with local rum cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Sea turtle beach patrols are strictly regulated — only licensed guides with official permits may conduct them. Groups are limited to 6–8 people. Photography with flash is prohibited on the beach. February sightings are not guaranteed but leatherback season begins this month — manage expectations accordingly. Mosquito repellent is essential in Tortuguero.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tortuguero — early birdwatching walk along the jungle trails with the lodge's resident naturalist guide. Tortuguero is a world-class birding destination with over 300 species including the great green macaw, keel-billed toucan, and various herons and kingfishers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private boat transfer back through the jungle waterways to the mainland (approximately 2 hours). Private luxury vehicle transfer to San José (approximately 2.5 hours). Check into a premium San José hotel for the final night (Hotel Grano de Oro, Kura Design Villas, or equivalent).
day_by_day.evening: Farewell gourmet dinner at San José's finest restaurant — Sikwa Restaurant (indigenous-inspired cuisine) or Restaurante Nuema — featuring the best of Costa Rican gastronomy. Celebrate the journey with a premium wine pairing and traditional Costa Rican desserts. Optional: evening visit to the National Theater of Costa Rica (Teatro Nacional) if a performance is scheduled.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at Tortuga Lodge — full tropical breakfast spread with fresh fruits, eggs, and specialty Costa Rican coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at a premium restaurant in Puerto Viejo de Sarapiquí or en route to San José — fresh local cuisine and craft beverages
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Sikwa Restaurant or equivalent premium San José restaurant — tasting menu celebrating Costa Rica's diverse culinary heritage with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Confirm private transfer from Tortuguero to San José well in advance. Alternatively, book a charter flight from Tortuguero airstrip directly to San José Juan Santamaría Airport (30 minutes) for a seamless luxury transfer. Use the afternoon drive to purchase last-minute souvenirs — look for artisanal crafts, local coffee, and chocolate in San José's Mercado Central or Barrio Escalante boutiques.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final morning in San José. Explore the Barrio Escalante neighborhood — Costa Rica's culinary and arts hub — for a premium breakfast at a specialty coffee shop. Visit the Jade Museum (Museo del Jade) or Pre-Columbian Gold Museum (Museo del Oro) for a cultural farewell to Costa Rica.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final luxury shopping at La Sabana boutiques or Multiplaza Escazú mall. Purchase premium Costa Rican coffee, artisanal chocolate, and handcrafted souvenirs. Private transfer to Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO) with ample time for check-in and departures. Enjoy the airport's premium lounge before your flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from San José Juan Santamaría International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of eco-adventure, wildlife encounters, and luxury immersion across Costa Rica's most spectacular landscapes.

meals.breakfast: Premium breakfast in Barrio Escalante — specialty Costa Rican pour-over coffee, fresh pastries, tropical fruit bowls, and avocado toast at Café Rojo or Café de los Deseos
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at a premium Escazú or San José restaurant — El Cielo Restaurant or Chez Christophe — featuring French-Costa Rican fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before international departure for check-in, immigration, and security at SJO. The airport has a premium lounge (Club El Dorado) accessible with certain credit cards or for purchase. Pack all biological materials (seeds, plants, soil) are strictly prohibited for export from Costa Rica — customs checks are thorough. Consider purchasing pre-packaged premium Costa Rican coffee and single-origin chocolate as gifts at duty-free.
